narrative.text: The first page of the draft third report of Committee A of the Fifty-fourth World Health Assembly (May 2001, Russian version), listing its meetings and chairs and recommending two resolutions: scaling up the response to HIV/AIDS and the WHO medicines strategy. Some OCR errors appear in names.

The preamble of the draft World Health Assembly resolution on scaling up the response to HIV/AIDS, describing AIDS as an unprecedented crisis and affirming the right to health and non-discriminatory access to care. It notes the harm of stigma, the importance of prevention and care together, and the existence of affordable drugs for opportunistic infections.

Continues the preamble of the HIV/AIDS resolution, noting that antiretroviral therapy reduces mortality and that price cuts have widened access, that health systems are overstretched, and that humanitarian programmes must protect refugees and displaced people. It welcomes the planned global fund for AIDS and health and refers to regional declarations and UN human rights resolutions.

Acknowledges the roles of UNAIDS, the UN Secretary-General and WHO, then urges Member States to make HIV/AIDS a top priority with adequate resources. Calls include ensuring young people know how to protect themselves, broadening multisectoral responses, reducing stigma, pursuing high treatment standards, involving people living with HIV and developing a continuum of care.

Continues the HIV/AIDS resolution's calls to Member States on research investment, financial and technical support, pharmaceutical and intellectual property policies to widen drug access and support for a global fund. It then asks the Director-General to provide normative guidance and technical support, strengthen health systems and monitor drug resistance and adverse reactions.
Ends the HIV/AIDS resolution by asking the Director-General to help create a global fund for HIV/AIDS and health with transparent governance including civil society.

Opens the draft World Health Assembly resolution on the WHO medicines strategy, recalling earlier resolutions and the strategy's four objectives: policy, access, quality and safety, and rational use. It notes the burden of diseases such as malaria, HIV/AIDS and TB on the poor and affirms the right to health and WHO's framework for access to essential medicines.

Continues the preamble of the medicines strategy resolution, noting that access depends heavily on price because most people in developing countries pay out of pocket, and that a third of humanity lacks essential medicines. It acknowledges WHO's leadership on essential medicines and calls for further assessment of how trade agreements affect access and local production. The footnote title is garbled in the OCR text.

Urges Member States in the medicines strategy resolution to improve access to medicines in line with international law, cooperate on the UN human rights resolution, implement earlier resolutions, and strengthen policies on generics and intellectual property. It also asks for financial and technical support for countries in need. It then asks the Director-General to work with partners on affordability and explore global voluntary monitoring of drug prices.

Continues the Director-General's tasks under the medicines strategy resolution, including supporting drug monitoring systems for resistance and adverse reactions, studying the health effects of trade agreements, helping national regulators ensure quality, continuing work on traditional medicine and reporting to the next Assembly.
